title: Rate–distortion tradeoff for distributed lossy source coding
formal: Determine \(F_{\mathrm{RD}}(\mathrm{P},d_{1},d_{2},D_{1},D_{2},\lambda )=\inf _{(R_{1},R_{2})\in R(\mathrm{P},d_{1},d_{2},D_{1},D_{2})}[\lambda R_{1}+(1- \lambda )R_{2}]\) for every finite-alphabet memoryless source pair, finite per-symbol distortion tables, feasible distortion targets and \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), where R is the separate-encoder joint-decoder rate–distortion region defined below.
context:
Separate encoders cannot coordinate their descriptions by inspecting one another’s source blocks, even though the decoder can use both descriptions together. Correlation can therefore save rate while creating a tradeoff between the two encoders. Allowing a controlled reconstruction loss gives a different problem from exact recovery.

This card represents the lower boundary of the rate region by its minimum weighted rate. Distortion targets below the minimum attainable expected per-symbol distortion are excluded explicitly, so the target stays finite. The numerical tolerance is in compression-rate units, with the distortion constraints themselves kept exact. The known lossless and single-sided side-information cases do not determine the general two-source lossy tradeoff.
why: The basic unresolved limit of compressing correlated information without coordination between encoders.

definitions: The source alphabets \(X_{1},X_{2}\) and reproduction alphabets \(\hat\{X\}_{1},\hat\{X\}_{2}\) are nonempty finite sets. P is an arbitrary real joint probability table on \(X_{1}\times X_{2}\), and the pairs \((X_{1},t,X_{2},t)\) are independent draws from P over time. Each \(d_{i}:X_{i}\times \hat\{X\}_{i}\to \mathbb{R} \ge 0\) is a finite-valued distortion table. Let \(\mathrm{P}_{i}\) be the marginal law and \(D_{i},\min =\sum _{x\in X_{i}}\mathrm{P}_{i}(x) \min _{z\in \hat\{X\}_{i}}d_{i}(x,z)\). The domain has finite \(D_{i}\ge D_{i},\min\) and real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\). An n-block code has two deterministic maps \(f_{i}:X_{i}^{n}\to \{1,\ldots ,M_{i},n\}\) and one deterministic decoder mapping the two indices to \((\hat\{X\}_{1}^{n},\hat\{X\}_{2}^{n})\). Encoder i observes only its own source block; the encoders cannot communicate or see the other block. Define average distortion \(\Delta _{i},n=(1/n)\sum _{t=1}^{n} E[d_{i}(X_{i},t,\hat\{X\}_{i},t)]\), with expectation over the iid source pair. A nonnegative rate pair is achievable if, along \(n_{j}\to \infty\), codes have \(\limsup _{j} (\log _{2}M_{i},n_{j})/n_{j}\le R_{i}\) and \(\limsup _{j} \Delta _{i},n_{j}\le D_{i}\) for \(i=1,2\). R is the closure of these pairs. There are no computational restrictions, extra side information, interaction, excess-distortion probability requirements or variable-length codewords. Predetermined time sharing is allowed. Feasibility follows by transmitting both source blocks and using a minimum-distortion reproduction at each symbol. Below \(D_{i},\min\) the region is empty, so those parameters are expressly outside this real-valued function’s domain. \(F_{\mathrm{RD}}\) is finite, nonnegative and measured in weighted bits per source pair. The region is convex and upward closed; all its nonnegative lower support values describe its lower rate boundary. The tables are mathematical real objects, not finite-input algorithms.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous real-valued function g on all source and distortion tables above, all finite \(D_{i}\ge D_{i},\min\), and all real \(\lambda \in [0,1]\), and prove in Lean that |\(g- F_{\mathrm{RD}}(\mathrm{P},d_{1},d_{2},D_{1},D_{2},\lambda )|\le 1/100\) pointwise throughout that domain, in the units stated in the definitions. The answer must establish lower and upper bounds with this uniform error guarantee. An exact determination also qualifies. A finite set of sample values, an uncertified plot, or a restatement of the defining optimization or limit does not determine the curve. No predetermined formula grammar or polynomial evaluation-time requirement is imposed. This numerical acceptance criterion does not assert exact equality with a conjectured curve.

sentences: Two correlated memoryless sources are compressed by separate encoders and reconstructed by one joint decoder.
Each source has its own expected per-symbol distortion limit.
The target is the minimum weighted sum of rates over the full rate–distortion region for every feasible parameter choice.
Lean acceptance allows absolute error 0.01 bits per source pair in that weighted rate, while preserving the exact distortion constraints.
The formulation specifies the numerical curve without requiring a single-letter formula or an efficient encoding algorithm.
